correctness.rationale: The density is 1+delta alpha² g(u)g(v) with g antisymmetric on reflection. The absolute maximum of g is 1 for alpha<=2 and sqrt(2/alpha) exp(alpha/4-1/2) otherwise, so nonnegativity gives exactly the claimed admissibility interval. The u-derivative of the conditional CDF for nonzero alpha and positive delta has sign alpha(1-2u)²-2. For alpha>2 it is strictly positive on an interior interval near an endpoint; for alpha<=2 it is nonpositive everywhere. Negative coupling fails at u=1/2, and the independent cases are SI. Rank correlation is 12 delta h(alpha)²; on the positive upper boundary for nonzero alpha<=2 its envelope strictly increases because h(alpha)/alpha is the integral of x times the average of exp(t alpha x) over 0<=t<=1. The actual alpha=0 member has zero correlation, even though the rescaled boundary limit is 1/3. At alpha>2 the positive envelope has derivative sign opposite Q(s), s=sqrt(alpha)/2. Direct differentiation yields Q'(s)=s²(2s²-1)exp(-s²), and Q(0)=0 with positive limit at infinity, giving one root beyond 1/sqrt(2) and strict unimodality there. Its tail tends to zero. This yields both sharp maxima, the negative mirror bound, and exactly two upper-boundary shapes at intermediate high correlations. Proportionality of the rank-one factors for different nonzero shapes is impossible by the linear and quadratic Taylor coefficients in u(1-u), so the two copulas are distinct. An independent integrated-power-series computation in alpha reproduced both maxima and the maximizing shape.
residual_risks: Numerical calculations do not prove global uniqueness. Some frozen sign diagnostics use coupling magnitudes outside the admissible interval; the analytic derivative factorization gives the sign for every admissible coupling and does not depend on those samples.
Two-branch uniqueness is only on the positive admissibility boundary, and the ceilings are not universal over all copulas.

value.rationale: The substantive result is not the small numerical refinement of 0.5866. This family was designed for larger rank dependence, and the separate sharp SI ceiling identifies exactly when high correlation rules out monotone conditional responses even though positive quadrant dependence remains. The exact two-branch conclusion also shows rank correlation alone does not identify the boundary copula in that range. The natural dependence and conditional-order constraints motivate the optimization before computing it.
residual_risks: The ceilings and nonidentifiability are specific to the stated family; no empirical model-fitting advantage or universal SI limitation is claimed.
